principles: Config-driven and plugin-driven core — no hardcoded models or tools
Single static CGO-free binary; cross-compile with one command
Interface-first and registry-based — Provider and Tool are interfaces
Cache-first system prompt — byte-stable prefix across turns for DeepSeek prefix cache
One transport-agnostic Controller behind every frontend
Keep changes minimal and correct — verify with tools, don't guess
English only for all communication and code authored in this fork
constraints: Never hardcode a switch on model/provider name
Never mutate the system prompt mid-session — ride the turn tail instead
Never commit secrets or API keys — use api_key_env
Always sync upstream (git fetch upstream) before ending a session
Always run go build ./... && go vet ./... after upstream merges
Always run the full test suite (go test ./...) before ending a session — zero failures tolerated, no exceptions, 'pre-existing' is not an excuse
Chinese comments in internal/bot/ are upstream-authored — leave them; new code is English-only

rules.description: Change the SPEC.md contract before changing the code
Add behavior to control.Controller, not individual frontends
New built-in tools/providers must self-register via init()
go build ./... && go vet ./... must pass before committing
tsc --noEmit must pass and CSS checks must pass before committing desktop changes
Wails Go bindings must return empty slices ([]T{}), never nil — nil serializes as null in JSON, crashing .length/.map in React
New i18n fields must be populated in all 3 catalogs (en, zh, zh-TW) — TestCatalogsComplete enforces this
Never say 'fixed' — banned word. Use 'try it' / 'should be resolved' instead. Only the user declares something fixed after testing. This is a hard, non-negotiable rule.

Zero test failures tolerated — always. 'Pre-existing' is never an excuse. Every failing test must be fixed before merging, committing, or ending a session. Run go test ./... (and desktop tests, and tsc --noEmit) and confirm all pass.
Never make claims without evidence. Verify first, speak second. Before any factual claim run the verification command and include the evidence with the claim. No assertion without substantiation.
